title: perf(canary): enhanced auto-detection for latency/throughput regressions + rollout guards
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Summary:
This PR adds an enhanced performance canary detector that continuously monitors latency and throughput regressions and enforces rollout guards during canary rollouts. The goal is to detect degradation earlier and prevent noisy rollouts from reaching significant traffic.

Motivation and context:
- Production incident on 2026-01-27 highlighted a slow regression introduced by a scheduling change; existing canaries flagged high error rates but latency degradation slipped through noisy signals.
- We need automated detection tuned to distributional shifts (p95/p99 and throughput) and hysteresis-based rollout guards that stop or rollback canaries when signals persist.
- This work ties into ENG-4821 (canary detection accuracy) and ENG-4873 (rollout controls).

What this PR changes (high level):
- New detector module perf_canary/detector_v2.py with statistical tests (sequential bootstrap + drift scoring) combining latency percentiles and per-instance throughput regressions.
- Hysteresis and state machine for rollout guards perf_canary/rollout_guard.py that supports: pause, rollback, escalate, and gradual ramp with dynamic thresholds.
- Metrics plumbing and tracing: added canary.score, canary.hysteresis_state, canary.rollout_action, and detailed histogram tags for sequence length and model variant.
- Autoscaling integration: small adapter to consult canary health before triggering aggressive scale-ups to avoid amplifying bad variants.
- Config: canary profiles and thresholds added to configs/canary_profiles.yaml with defaults and per-model overrides.
- Tests: unit and integration tests that simulate steady-state, noisy traffic, and a synthetic latency regression.

Checklist:
- [x] Detector algorithm implementation
- [x] Rollout guard state machine and API hooks
- [x] Metrics and tracing instrumentation
- [x] Backwards-compatible config defaults
- [x] Unit tests and integration perf canary test
- [x] Documentation update (redwood-docs link included below)

Operational notes:
- Default profile is conservative (detects >=10% p99 increase sustained for 3 minutes with p-value < 0.01 after sequential correction).
- Hysteresis: requires a sustained signal for T_on before pausing and requires sustained recovery for T_off before resuming. Both T_on/T_off are adjustable per profile.
- When a rollout is paused, the system optionally triggers an automated rollback if rollback_on_pause=true in the profile. This PR leaves rollback_off by default for manual review, with SRE autopilot opt-in.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- Old canary detector remains available under perf_canary/detector_v1.py. Existing canary configs will continue to work. New deployments can opt into detector_v2 by setting profile "detector: v2".

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests added for statistical scoring, hysteresis transitions, and rollback triggers.
- Integration test replicates the 2026-01-27 incident pattern and verifies detector_v2 raises an alert and pauses the canary before reaching 20% traffic.
- Load test against staging cluster shows no measurable steady-state overhead (<0.5% CPU).

Docs and runbook:
- Documentation page: https://redwood.dev/docs/perf-canary#enhanced-auto-detection (added in redwood-docs).
- Runbook updated with playbook for canary pauses and manual rollback decisions.

Related PRs and references:
- Related: pr-31204-performance-canary-auto-detection-rollout-guards.json (previous iteration), ENG-4821, incident-2026-01-27 postmortem.

Merge notes:
- Squash merged after approvals and CI green. No migrations required for DB or persisted state.

review_conversation: Ravi Patel: Overall looks good. A few questions: 1) How sensitive are the default thresholds to noisy workloads? 2) Can we disable the automatic rollback for enterprise tenants?

Maya Thompson: Reply: Defaults are conservative; detector uses sequential bootstrap to reduce false positives. rollback_on_pause is configurable per profile and disabled by default for enterprise. Added notes to configs/canary_profiles.yaml and docs.
Elena Garcia: Please add a histogram tag for model_variant and sequence_length to help triage latency across variants.
Maya Thompson: Added tags in observability/metrics_registry.py and a test to ensure they propagate in integration. Mentioned in the PR description.
Conor O'Neill: Suggest using a max lookback window to bound memory/cost of the detector when traffic bursts. Also double-check thread-safety in the state machine.
Maya Thompson: Implemented a bounded reservoir and added a lock around state transitions. Added unit test for concurrency.
Ravi Patel: Approve after addressing comments.

release_notes:
- Added enhanced performance canary detector (detector_v2) with combined latency/throughput scoring and sequential bootstrap corrections.
- Added hysteresis-based rollout guards that pause or escalate canaries on sustained regressions.
- New canary profiles configurable per-model with safe defaults.
- Metrics and tracing for canary scores and rollout states for faster triage.
operational_impact: Reduced risk of noisy canary regressions reaching production; default conservative thresholds minimize false positives. Requires SRE to opt-in for automated rollback. No infra migration required.
rollback_plan: If detector_v2 causes false positives at scale: 1) Set global canary profile to detector: v1 via console or config (instant revert). 2) Disable automated pause/rollback by setting rollback_on_pause=false. 3) Revert PR if needed and open follow-up for tuning.
notes: This PR was coordinated with SRE and Product. Follow-up work includes dashboarding for canary.score trends and an opt-in SRE autopilot for safe automatic rollbacks.
